A1.justification: Both PDFs describe FAHNES by the same authors. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original FAHNES results on synthetic hypergraphs, ModelNet40, Manifold40 meshes, and QM9, together with ablations and generated samples.

after.justification: v2 reports original hypergraph and mesh results, component ablations, and newly added graph point cloud experiments, including numerical and visual outcomes.

M1.justification: The core coarsening, budget refinement, feature generation, and Local PPGN architecture remain. v2 adds a direct graph-generation variant initialized from one node in Section 3.6 and changes the stated sampling distribution for flow-matching time t from uniform to log-normal in Appendix E.1. These are bounded adaptations of the existing framework.

E1.justification: QM9 molecular generation, including categorical atom and bond features, is removed entirely. v2 adds Airplane and Bench graph point cloud generation using sampled surface points and neighborhood connectivity, a distinct topology-generation task despite reusing the mesh shape classes. The five featureless datasets and two featured mesh datasets remain.

E2.justification: The QM9 comparison against DiGress, DisCo, Cometh, and DeFoG disappears. v2 instead evaluates DiGress and DeFoG adapted to mixed discrete/continuous point cloud generation, reporting out-of-memory outcomes for both. The featureless comparator roster and sequential mesh baseline remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The shared training budget changes from a stated 24 hours in v1 Appendix F to one million steps in v2 Appendix D; this establishes a reported protocol revision, not a known increase in computation. New point cloud evaluation introduces graph-statistic MMDs and an aggregate Ratio metric. Existing dataset splits, model dimensions, and 25 sampling steps are retained.

E4.justification: v2 adds budget and OT-coupling ablations on featured Airplane and Bench meshes, directly testing their contribution to feature generation in Tables 5 and 10. It removes v1's four validation-trajectory plots in Appendix G and the Section 4 diagnostic reporting only 30% valid bipartite outputs from graph generators. Existing featureless component ablations remain.

E5.justification: v1 provides point estimates without an explicit repeated-run count or numerical uncertainty. v2 Appendix H defines reported intervals as mean plus or minus twice the standard deviation over five runs and applies this broadly to FAHNES comparisons and ablations. This is newly documented uncertainty reporting, not evidence that the run count increased.

E6.justification: Reported FAHNES validity changes from 81.4%, 100%, and 82.8% to 87.8%, 99.5%, and 89.7% for SBM, Ego, and Tree. These are revised summaries under changed training and reporting settings. v2 also adds point cloud, mesh-ablation, and baseline-centrality results while removing QM9 outcomes. Some later values conflict internally: Bench point cloud Ratio is 84.423 in Table 3 but 73.279 in Table 8.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 revises the likelihood factorization and conditional-independence statement, placing budget fractions and refined features in the refinement distribution conditioned on the expanded graph. Appendix A.2 adds Proposition 12 and a proof that OT matching reduces summed squared endpoint distances. The averaging proof, marginal-preservation argument, and complexity analysis are substantially retained.

C1.justification: v1 foregrounds featured hypergraph generation across geometric and molecular domains and acknowledges limited molecular competitiveness. v2 broadens the central contribution to direct graph and hypergraph generation, foregrounds meshes and point clouds, and explicitly claims operation at scales beyond prior flat models. Its abstract also replaces competitive performance with a state-of-the-art claim.

C2.justification: v1 explains molecular weaknesses through accumulated hierarchical errors, categorical features, incompatible molecular techniques, and backbone tradeoffs. v2 replaces this discussion with limitations concerning very large structures, richer feature distributions, and training expense. Its ablation interpretation also becomes more qualified about dataset-dependent OT benefits while adding conclusions about the components' importance for feature generation.

D1.justification: v2 documents point cloud construction using 1024 surface samples, three-nearest-neighbor connections, and largest-component filtering, plus associated model settings and comparator adaptations. QM9's 20,000-sample evaluation instructions and molecular hyperparameters disappear. Most architecture, hardware, coarsening, and training/sampling documentation is retained, alongside the revised training-budget disclosure.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations covering a graph-generation survey, circuit modeling, cellular transformers, and rectified-flow training, while removing several application and molecular-evaluation references. The central relationship to HYGENE, iterative local expansion, and feature-aware generative modeling remains, with increased emphasis on graph scalability.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, method overview, and limitations receive substantial rewrites. Experiments gain explicit setup, results, ablation, and limitations subsections; appendices are extensively reordered, and flow-matching exposition is consolidated there. v1's incorrect HYGENE running header is also corrected.

P2.justification: The framework diagram is redrawn with budget annotations and a mesh trajectory. Main tables are condensed, fuller comparisons are assembled in Appendix H, and mesh tables are restructured. The clique/star illustration, four validation plots, and molecular panel are removed; point cloud tables and panels are added. Existing coarsening examples are relocated rather than newly introduced.

improvement.justification: Five-run uncertainty reporting, featured-mesh ablations, and clearer exposition strengthen v2. However, removing QM9 eliminates the only evaluation of categorical node and edge features, which exposed weak performance. Numerical reliability also suffers: Table 7 reverses the sequential mesh baseline assignments retained in Section 4.2, and Tables 3 and 8 disagree on Bench point cloud results. These substantive gains and losses prevent a confident overall quality judgment.
